proposal.hypothesis: A 256-thread CTA with a 128-source tile lets each staged source chunk serve twice as many target threads as a 128-thread CTA, potentially reducing CTA scheduling overhead while using 2048 bytes of shared memory. The smaller tile doubles source-tile iterations versus the selected parent, so added synchronization and iteration overhead may offset that reuse; only the official correctness checks and timing can determine the result.

retained: Set the launch block and items_per_block to 256, with 2048 bytes of dynamic shared memory for 128 compact source records.
Use 128-source chunks cooperatively staged by the 256-thread CTA; retain one target and force accumulator per thread.
Preserve bounds for partial source chunks and target tails, keep every thread participating in both barriers, exclude self-interactions by global particle index, and write each valid target once.
